newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs quietly await signals from U.S..
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs quietly await signals from U.S..

text.p: Belgian OLOs edged up in quiet trading on Tuesday, awaiting domestic inflation data later this morning and figures from across the Atlantic in the afternoon.
"We're waiting for the U.S. figures," said one dealer, adding, "Investors hope to get paper cheaper in the coming days (than today).

March durable goods orders, due at 1230 GMT, are seen unchanged after a 1.5 percent rise in February, while the U.S. consumer confidence index at 1400 GMT is seen barely changed at 118.4. On the domestic front Belgian April inflation is seen slowing to 1.37 percent year-on-year from 1.46 percent in March.

OLOs should benefit in the days ahead from the reinvestment of coupon payments today on more than 700 billion Belgian francs of outstanding paper, dealers said, which in turn could send the 10-year yield spread over Bunds down from its current 15 bps.

Some thought investors might begin buying before Friday's monthly U.S. jobs data, though another said there was no immediate hurry to buy. Around 50 billion francs of coupons are due to be paid by the Treasury on OLO 13 (7.00 pct April 1999) and OLO 14 (7.25 pct April 2004).
By 0900 GMT the benchmark March 2007 OLO was yielding an unchanged 6.04 percent.
Front month OLO futures stood 17 bps higher at 120.07.
